title: Certify v0.9.0: Kelmans' 1984 problem on 3-vertex path packings in cubic 3-connected graphs, verified exhaustively through 22 vertices — 6,339,157 graphs, two independent pipelines, 53,356 replayable certificates
description: Let lambda(G) be the maximum number of vertex-disjoint 3-vertex paths in a graph G; counting vertices gives lambda(G) <= floor(v(G)/3). Kelmans asked in 1984 (Problem 1.10 of arXiv:0910.2766) whether equality holds for every cubic 3-connected graph. Specialized to orders divisible by 3 this is the Akiyama-Kano P_3-factor conjecture, and a positive answer would give Reed's domination conjecture for cubic 3-connected graphs. The problem is open, and no computational verification of it at any order appears in the record. This release supplies one, and is to our knowledge the first recorded computational verification of the problem at any order. For EVERY 3-connected cubic graph on at most 22 vertices — all 6,339,157 of them — lambda(G) = floor(v(G)/3), together with the applicable strong forms of Kelmans' equivalence theorem 3.1: (z2),(z3),(z7),(z8) at orders 6, 12, 18; (t2) at 8, 14, 20; (f1),(f2) at 4, 10, 16 and (f1) at 22. Those equivalences are constructive, so a single failure at any of these orders would have produced an explicit cubic 3-connected graph of order divisible by 6 with no Lambda-factor, i.e. a counterexample to the conjecture; none was found. Graphs were generated with geng from nauty 2.9.3; generated and filtered counts equal the published enumerations at every order (OEIS A002851 and Brinkmann-Goedgebeur-McKay; OEIS A204198 at every order and McKay-Royle at orders 10-20). Two pipelines sharing no code — different connectivity tests, different search orders, both negative-controlled — agree on every count and report zero failures. THE PUBLIC UNIT IS CERTIFICATES PLUS STANDARD-LIBRARY CHECKERS: 53,356 Lambda-factor certificates ship (all 43,580 through order 22 and 9,776 at order 24), each carrying only a graph6 string, the vertex triples forming the paths, and the avoided vertices; two independently written stdlib-only checkers re-derive everything from the graph6 string alone — own decoder, cubicity, 3-connectivity re-proved by exhaustive vertex-pair deletion, each triple a path, triples plus avoided vertices a partition with |avoided| = n mod 3 — and every certificate passes both, with zero rejections, on CPython 3.9.6 and 3.14.2. SCOPE, STATED PLAINLY: 24 vertices is SEARCH-SIDE COMPLETE ONLY (98,101,019 3-connected cubic graphs, zero failures, counts matching the published enumeration) with NO independent recount, and is reported at that strength and no higher; strong form (f2) was not tested at order 22, and (z7),(z8) were not tested at order 24; the completeness of the geng enumeration is the load-bearing external assumption, mitigated by count agreement with two independent published enumerations; and the two searchers are specified in the paper but are not deposited, so a reader can re-check every positive answer they gave and reproduce the enumeration counts, but cannot re-run a sweep from this deposit alone. No finite computation resolves the conjecture, and none is claimed. Every component passed a three-lens adversarial review before release (claims-vs-artifacts with independent re-derivation of every count, replay audit with tamper controls, novelty and citation checks); the decision log ships as kelmans-paper/FIXLOG.md and the dated sweep as SWEEP-RECORD-KELMANS-2026-08-11.md. Computations carried out with Claude (Anthropic), directed by the author; the certificate checkers share no code with the searchers.
